name: OpenShell
description: OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for autonomous AI agents.
one_liner: A locked-down box for AI agents to work in — they can read files, install software, and call APIs, but only inside rules you set, so they can't leak passwords or wander onto the wrong server.
buyer: A platform or security lead at a company letting AI agents touch production systems, who needs proof (for auditors or customers) that an agent can't exfiltrate data or reach unapproved hosts.
business_use_cases: A healthcare software vendor runs its AI triage agents inside OpenShell so they can read patient records for their task but are policy-blocked from ever sending that data outside the hospital's network.
An agency running client coding agents overnight locks each one to only that client's repo and secrets, so a prompt-injection attack on one client can't touch another's credentials.
A cloud platform bundles OpenShell as a 'sandboxed agents' add-on so enterprise customers can check a compliance box without building their own isolation layer.

money_ideas.idea: Sell a hosted, managed OpenShell gateway with prebuilt SOC2/HIPAA policy templates for teams that don't want to run infrastructure themselves.
Offer paid policy-authoring and incident-review consulting to companies rolling out their first agent fleets.

steal_this: This weekend, package OpenShell with a starter 'no outbound internet except an allowlist, no home directory access' policy and ship it as a one-command safe sandbox for solo developers running overnight AI coding agents.
